copy.blurb:
FIFA World Cup 2026 on Sunday, evening UTC kickoff, brings Belgium and IR Iran together. The Desk's read disagrees with the market on the IR Iran side, by +12.0pp — and that disagreement is the Pick.

Public Elo rates Belgium 130 points higher than the other side (Belgium 1880, IR Iran 1750). The match model's logistic translates that Elo gap directly into a win-probability. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. No host, home-ground, or altitude adjustments apply here; the prior reads straight from Elo.

Three-way split from the model: Belgium to win at 53%, the draw at 22%, and IR Iran to win at 25%. The away side reads 25% on this distribution — the model's central case for IR Iran.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: Belgium to win at 67%, the draw at 22%, and IR Iran to win at 13%. Reading those three numbers as a probability distribution, the market's view is internally consistent. The disagreement with the model is concentrated on the IR Iran side — 13% on the market, 25% on the engine, a +12.0pp gap.

The +3pp Pick threshold isn't on the point estimate, it's on the 5th-percentile from a 100-sample bootstrap of the Elo prior plus bonuses. On IR Iran, that haircut lands the model at 20%; the market is at 13%. Even on the conservative reading, the gap is +7.2pp. The Desk's posture is that calibration sits with the closing market across recent fixtures — we're not claiming the market is generally wrong, only that this side, on this fixture, looks mispriced. Selection is the dimension this verdict adds value on.

The number above is the most recent read; it isn't frozen. With kickoff roughly 33 days out, the model is on the weekly refresh cadence; we'll move to daily once we cross the T-5d window. Injury news, the actual XI, and weather conditions at kickoff all feed back into the prior when they land. We republish on every refresh. The Desk surfaces edge; what to do with that surface is a reader's call.
drivers: Pre-tournament Elo gives IR Iran a stronger prior than the Polymarket line implies.
The +12.0pp gap clears our 3 percentage point threshold for a Pick.
Calibration sits with the closing market across recent fixtures, so selection is the lever.
Late-binding signals — form, confirmed XI, weather — re-evaluate closer to kickoff.
copy.summary: A +12.0pp gap across model and market on the IR Iran side. Our Elo prior, after host and altitude adjustments, rates IR Iran at 25%; Polymarket sits at 13%.
copy.title: Belgium v IR Iran · the model leans IR Iran
